trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Banff, Alberta, Canada
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek
experiences.description: Hike the Rockpile Trail and Lakeshore Trail at the stunning Moraine Lake, one of the most photographed lakes in Canada. The vivid blue glacial water framed by the Valley of the Ten Peaks is an unforgettable natural spectacle.
experiences.location: Moraine Lake Road, Banff National Park

day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary International Airport at 14:00. Take the Banff Airporter or On It Transit shuttle (budget option ~$30-40 CAD one-way) to Banff town. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge. Take a leisurely walk along Bow River Trail right in town to decompress and get your first taste of the Rockies scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Banff Avenue to get oriented. Head up to the free Bow River Falls viewpoint (short 10-minute walk from town center). Watch the sunset over the mountains from the bridge — no cost, stunning views.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Calgary airport before boarding the shuttle, or pack snacks
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Banff Avenue — vegetarian-friendly, hearty portions, budget-friendly mains around $15-18 CAD. Alternatively, pick up groceries at Nesters Market on Bear Street to stock up for the week and save money on breakfasts and lunches.

day_by_day.notes: Stop at a grocery store (Nesters Market or IGA) on your first evening to buy snacks, trail mix, sandwiches, and water bottles for the hikes ahead. This will significantly reduce daily food costs. Purchase a Parks Canada Day Pass or Annual Discovery Pass (~$10.50/day or $75.25/year) — required to enter Banff National Park.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike to Tunnel Mountain Summit Trail. This is a free, easy-to-moderate hike starting right from town (trailhead near St. Julien Road). The 2.3 km trail takes about 1–1.5 hours and rewards you with panoramic 360° views of the Bow Valley, Mount Rundle, and the town of Banff. Perfect orientation hike for your first full day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the free Roam Transit bus (Route 1, ~$2 CAD) to the Banff Visitor Centre to pick up free trail maps. Then explore the free Banff Park Museum (National Historic Site, ~$4 CAD entry) on Banff Avenue — a fascinating Victorian-era natural history museum. Afterward, walk to the beautiful Bow Falls viewpoint and the Hoodoos Viewpoint along the Bow River.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Cave and Basin National Historic Site exterior and boardwalk trails at dusk for a peaceful nature walk along the marsh. Watch for wildlife like elk near the river flats at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the lodge using groceries purchased last night — oatmeal, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on Tunnel Mountain — sandwiches and trail mix from Nesters Market
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. — pub-style food with great mountain views, burgers and mains around $18-22 CAD. Or opt for a self-cooked meal if your lodge has kitchen facilities.

day_by_day.notes: Roam Transit buses are extremely budget-friendly ($2/ride or $5/day pass) and connect most major Banff town attractions. Wear layers — mornings can be cool even in July. Carry bear spray (rentable from local outfitters for ~$10/day).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day lake adventure: Take the Roam Transit Route 8X (Lake Louise Express, ~$8 CAD each way) to Lake Louise. Arrive early (by 8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk the flat, stunning Lake Louise Lakeshore Trail (4.0 km return, free with Parks Canada pass) along the turquoise glacial lake with the Victoria Glacier as your backdrop. Optional extension: hike up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (14 km return, moderate) for incredible glacier views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Lake Louise, board the Moraine Lake shuttle from the Lake Louise overflow parking area (book in advance via Parks Canada reservation system, ~$8 CAD return). Experience the Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — hike the short but spectacular Rockpile Trail (0.8 km, easy) for the iconic postcard view, then continue on the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) hugging the brilliant blue lake beneath the ten peaks. Absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff via Roam Transit. Rest your legs and enjoy a relaxed evening in town.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at the lodge before 7:00 AM departure — energy bars, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Moraine Lake lakeshore — this is essential as food at the lake is very expensive. Bring sandwiches, fruit, and snacks.
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street — a Banff institution with hearty comfort food, burgers and wraps around $18-20 CAD. Or self-cater for maximum savings.

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Moraine Lake Road is closed to private vehicles. You MUST pre-book the Parks Canada shuttle or Roam Transit Route 8X well in advance — these sell out weeks ahead. Book online at reservation.pc.gc.ca. Arrive at Lake Louise very early (before 8 AM) as the area gets extremely crowded by mid-morning. Bring sunscreen and a rain jacket just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Johnston Canyon — one of Banff's most magical trails. Take Roam Transit Route 9 (Bow Valley Parkway, ~$6 CAD) to Johnston Canyon. Hike the Lower Falls trail (2.7 km return, easy) through the dramatic limestone canyon on elevated catwalk platforms to the stunning 10-metre waterfall. Extend to the Upper Falls (5.4 km return, moderate) for an even more impressive 30-metre cascade. Start early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue past the Upper Falls to the Ink Pots (11.6 km return total from trailhead, moderate) — seven cold-water mineral springs that bubble up in vivid green, blue, and turquoise pools in an open meadow. This hidden gem is less crowded and absolutely worth the extra effort. Keep an eye out for wildlife including bears, deer, and birds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff on Roam Transit. Treat yourself to a soak at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16.50 CAD adult entry) — a well-earned reward for your legs after a full day of hiking. The outdoor pool sits at 1,585 metres elevation with incredible mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at lodge — eggs, toast, and coffee for energy before the long hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Ink Pots meadow — a perfect picnic spot. Bring substantial food as this is a long day.
meals.dinner: Whitebark Cafe on Bear Street — great casual cafe with affordable wraps, soups, and baked goods. Mains around $12-16 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon gets very busy on weekends — aim to be on the trail by 8:00 AM. The canyon catwalks can be slippery; wear proper hiking shoes with grip. The full Ink Pots hike is about 11.6 km return and takes 4-5 hours — budget your time accordingly. Hot Springs closes at 11 PM in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Sulphur Mountain Summit Trail (11 km return, moderate-strenuous, ~3-4 hours) — hike UP instead of taking the gondola to save $40+ CAD. The trail starts near the Hot Springs parking lot (Roam Transit Route 1). The climb rewards you with the same incredible panoramic views from the summit boardwalk at 2,281 metres, including views of seven mountain ranges. Once at the top, enjoy the free summit boardwalk and visit the Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station (National Historic Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Banff Gondola DOWN (one-way descent ticket ~$30 CAD, much cheaper than the return ticket). Back in town, rent a canoe or kayak on the Bow River from Banff Canoe Club (~$45/hour for a canoe shared between 2 people) and paddle the scenic stretch of the Bow River through the valley — a magical perspective of the surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the free Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies (free on certain evenings, otherwise ~$10 CAD) for local art and mountain history. Enjoy a final sunset walk along the Bow River Pathway.

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-catered breakfast before the big climb — oatmeal with nuts and honey, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at the Sulphur Mountain summit boardwalk with panoramic views — the ultimate lunch setting
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly at Bear Street Tavern — wood-fired pizzas around $20-24 CAD, a great value treat after a big hiking day. Share a pizza to save more.

day_by_day.notes: Hiking up Sulphur Mountain instead of taking the gondola both ways saves approximately $40-50 CAD per person — a huge budget win. Bring trekking poles if available as the descent can be hard on knees. The Banff Canoe Club rental is best enjoyed in the afternoon when the light on the mountains is golden. Book canoes in advance on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike: Fenland Trail Loop (2 km, easy, free) — a peaceful flat trail through a boreal forest near the Forty Mile Creek, excellent for wildlife spotting (beaver, elk, birds). This gentle walk is perfect for tired legs on departure day. Afterward, visit the free Cascade Gardens and the grounds of the Banff Administration Building for beautiful mountain-framed flower gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (store luggage at the hotel if needed). Browse the shops on Banff Avenue for any last-minute souvenirs — check out the Banff Trading Post for affordable keepsakes. Grab a final look at the iconic view of Cascade Mountain from the main street. Board your return shuttle to Calgary airport (book Banff Airporter or On It Transit in advance, ~$30-40 CAD).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Calgary or continue travels. Reflect on an incredible week in the Canadian Rockies!

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at the lodge — use up any remaining groceries to minimize waste and cost
meals.lunch: Evelyn's Coffee Bar on Banff Avenue — great affordable sandwiches, wraps, and coffee around $12-15 CAD. Perfect pre-departure meal.
meals.dinner: Airport meal in Calgary or packed snacks for travel

day_by_day.notes: Book your return shuttle at least 24-48 hours in advance as they fill up. Allow at least 2.5 hours travel time from Banff to Calgary airport plus check-in time. Use up any remaining trail snacks and groceries to avoid waste. Consider purchasing a National Parks Annual Discovery Pass if you plan to visit other Canadian parks this year — it pays for itself quickly.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge (~1.5 hours by shuttle or rental car). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Stroll along Banff Avenue, visit the Banff Visitor Centre to pick up trail maps and park passes, and take a short walk to Bow River Falls viewpoint for a gentle introduction to the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and enjoy your first evening in Banff. Walk along the Bow River Pathway at sunset for beautiful mountain views before heading to dinner.

meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the Calgary airport or pack snacks for the drive
meals.dinner: Elk & Oarsman Restaurant on Banff Avenue – mid-range pub-style Canadian dining with burgers, bison dishes, and local craft beers; approx. CAD $25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Banff Visitor Centre if you haven't already – it covers park entry fees for all 6 days and saves money. Confirm shuttle or car rental arrangements for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Hike & Canoe – Head to Lake Louise (~45 min drive) and hike the iconic Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (14 km round trip, moderate difficulty). Start early to beat crowds. Enjoy stunning views of the Victoria Glacier and turquoise lake waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, rent a canoe on Lake Louise from the Fairmont boathouse (~CAD $155/hour for a canoe). Paddle across the brilliantly blue glacial lake with the Victoria Glacier as your backdrop – a quintessential Banff experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff town. Freshen up at the lodge, then enjoy a leisurely evening stroll before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge or pick up pastries and coffee at Evelyn's Coffee Bar in Banff before departing
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch – sandwiches and snacks from Nesters Market in Banff (grocery store ideal for mid-range budgets). Eat at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only; soups and sandwiches ~CAD $15–20)
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace – locally sourced Canadian cuisine featuring Alberta bison, elk, and seasonal produce; approx. CAD $35–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Start hiking by 8:00 AM to avoid crowds at Lake Louise. Wear layers as the elevation can make it cooler at the top. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen. Canoe rentals are first-come, first-served.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek – Drive to Moraine Lake (~15 min from Lake Louise). Hike the Rockpile Trail first (short, 300 m) for the iconic panoramic view, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3 km easy loop) to soak in the vivid turquoise waters and towering peaks of the Valley of the Ten Peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Moraine Lake, drive back toward Banff and stop at the Johnston Canyon trailhead for a lighter afternoon walk. Explore the Lower Falls section of Johnston Canyon (2.7 km round trip, easy) – limestone walls and emerald pools make this a beautiful, less strenuous afternoon option.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Banff, visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (open until 5 PM – time permitting) or relax at the lodge before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge – aim to leave by 7:00 AM as Moraine Lake requires a reservation or early arrival for parking
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Moraine Lake – pick up supplies the evening before from Nesters Market. Alternatively, grab a quick bite at the Moraine Lake Lodge dining room (walk-ins limited; ~CAD $20–30)
meals.dinner: Coyotes Southwestern Grill – casual, flavourful Southwestern and Mediterranean-inspired dishes; great value at ~CAD $20–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Moraine Lake road requires a Parks Canada reservation or you must arrive before 6:00 AM or use the Parks Canada shuttle from Banff or Lake Louise. Book the shuttle in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca. This is one of the most photographed lakes in the world – worth the early start!

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Athabasca Glacier Walk – Depart early for the full-day drive along the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), one of the world's most scenic roads. Stop at Peyto Lake viewpoint (stunning turquoise teardrop-shaped lake), Bow Lake, and Crowfoot Glacier along the way north toward the Columbia Icefield.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre and walk onto the Athabasca Glacier via a guided Glacier Adventure tour (Ice Explorer bus; ~CAD $59/person) or hike the free Forefield Trail along the glacier's edge. Visit the Glacier Skywalk (~CAD $32/person) for a glass-floored walkway over a 280 m cliff with icefield views. Begin the scenic drive back to Banff, stopping at Mistaya Canyon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by early evening. Rest tired legs and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge before departure by 7:30 AM
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake picnic area – scenic and budget-friendly
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's – casual Cajun-inspired comfort food in a relaxed setting; approx. CAD $20–30 per person. Great for refuelling after a long day.

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion (~8–10 hours). Fill up your gas tank in Banff before leaving – there are limited fuel stops on the Parkway. Bring warm layers even in July as the Athabasca Glacier area is significantly colder. Book the Ice Explorer in advance online to secure your spot.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk Hike – Ride the Banff Gondola (~CAD $65/person) to the summit of Sulphur Mountain (2,281 m) for 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley. Walk the 1 km Summit Boardwalk to Sanson Peak and the historic weather observatory. Alternatively, hike up Sulphur Mountain Trail (9.4 km round trip, moderate) to save the gondola fee and earn the views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After descending, visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~CAD $16/person) located just below the gondola – a perfect way to soak tired muscles in naturally heated mineral waters with stunning mountain views. Spend 1–2 hours relaxing in the pools.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Banff townsite for souvenir shopping along Banff Avenue. Enjoy a final celebratory dinner at a slightly elevated restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Sky Bistro at the top of the gondola – splurge on the breakfast/brunch option with panoramic mountain views; approx. CAD $25–40 per person (worth it for the experience!)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Hot Springs café or pick up wraps and snacks from Banff Avenue Brewing Co. taproom
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse – Alberta beef steakhouse with a lively atmosphere; approx. CAD $45–70 per person. A great mid-range splurge to celebrate the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and towel for the Hot Springs – rentals are available on-site if needed. The gondola is very popular in July; book tickets online in advance to avoid long queues. If hiking up, allow 2–2.5 hours for the ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk (Full Experience) – Revisit Johnston Canyon for the full trail experience: hike past the Lower Falls and Upper Falls to reach the Ink Pots (8.4 km round trip, moderate). The Ink Pots are seven cold mineral springs that bubble up through the ground in vivid green and blue hues – a magical and lesser-visited highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a final afternoon. Visit the Banff Park Museum (National Historic Site; ~CAD $4/person) – a beautiful 1903 log building with fascinating natural history displays. Take a final peaceful walk along the Bow River Trail or Vermilion Lakes for wildlife spotting (elk, beavers, and waterfowl are common).
day_by_day.evening: Pack bags and enjoy a relaxed final dinner in Banff before preparing for departure or a final night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Whitebark Café – cozy café with excellent coffee, fresh pastries, and breakfast bowls; approx. CAD $12–20 per person
meals.lunch: Pack a light trail lunch for the Ink Pots hike – energy bars, fruit, and sandwiches from Nesters Market
meals.dinner: Bear Street Tavern – casual wood-fired pizza and pasta with a great atmosphere; approx. CAD $20–35 per person. Perfect relaxed farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can be busier in the afternoon – aim to start the Ink Pots hike by 8:30–9:00 AM. The full trail to the Ink Pots adds significant distance beyond the waterfalls, so wear proper footwear. Vermilion Lakes at sunset is one of the best wildlife and photography spots in Banff – don't miss it on your last evening.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel time from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge is approximately 1.5 hours. Enjoy the scenic Trans-Canada Highway drive through the foothills as your first taste of the Canadian Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Banff Mountain Lodge, check in, and settle into your luxury suite. Take a leisurely self-guided stroll along the Bow River Pathway through downtown Banff to acclimate to the mountain air and altitude. Browse the boutiques along Banff Avenue and visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a gentle, enriching introduction to the region.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a short walk to a premier Banff restaurant. Decompress on your private balcony with views of the surrounding peaks as the alpenglow lights up Mount Rundle.

meals.lunch: N/A — traveling; grab a light snack at Calgary Airport or en route
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort Hotel — Banff's only AAA Four Diamond fine dining restaurant, offering an exquisite tasting menu with locally inspired Canadian cuisine and an award-winning wine cellar. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Upon check-in, ask the concierge to confirm all upcoming activity bookings and arrange private transfers where needed. Request an early breakfast service for Day 2 as Moraine Lake access requires an early start. Hydrate well on arrival day — Banff sits at 1,383 m elevation and mild altitude effects are common.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek — Depart by 06:00 via private transfer to beat the crowds and secure access to Moraine Lake (private vehicle access is restricted; shuttle or resort booking required). Hike the Rockpile Trail for the iconic panoramic view of the turquoise lake framed by the Valley of the Ten Peaks, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail for a full immersive experience. The 5 km round-trip lakeshore hike is moderate and suitable for most fitness levels, with stunning reflections in the glacially fed waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the trek, enjoy a canoe rental on Moraine Lake — paddle the impossibly blue waters surrounded by towering peaks for an unforgettable luxury experience. Return to Banff Mountain Lodge by early afternoon for a refresh. Optionally, visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a restorative soak in mineral-rich thermal waters with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Sky Bistro atop Sulphur Mountain (accessible via gondola) or at a rooftop bar downtown, followed by dinner at one of Banff's finest establishments.

meals.breakfast: Early in-room continental breakfast or packed gourmet breakfast box arranged by the hotel concierge the night before — to be enjoyed en route or at the lake.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch curated by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, charcuterie, local cheeses, and sparkling water enjoyed lakeside at Moraine Lake.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace — celebrated farm-to-table dining featuring Alberta bison, wild game, and seasonal Rocky Mountain ingredients in a warm, rustic-luxe setting in downtown Banff.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road typically opens late May and closes in October. Private resort shuttles or pre-booked park-and-ride passes are mandatory — your concierge should arrange this in advance. Bring bear spray (available to rent/purchase in Banff), layered clothing, and sturdy hiking boots. Weather at the lake can be 5–8°C cooler than Banff town.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Hike & Canoe — Depart by 07:30 via private transfer to Lake Louise (45 minutes from Banff). Begin with the iconic Plain of Six Glaciers Trail, a 14 km round-trip moderate hike that ascends above Lake Louise past the Victoria Glacier, offering sweeping views of the Beehive peaks and the emerald lake far below. The trail leads to the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse, a beloved mountain hut serving hot drinks and light fare.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Lake Louise and treat yourself to a luxury canoe experience on the lake itself — rent a premium canoe from the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise boathouse and paddle the impossibly turquoise waters with the Victoria Glacier as your backdrop. This is one of the most iconic and photogenic experiences in all of Canada. Afterward, enjoy afternoon tea inside the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by private transfer. Enjoy a quiet evening with a spa treatment at the hotel's wellness facilities, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Fairview Bar & Restaurant inside the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise — elegant lakeside dining with floor-to-ceiling mountain views. Arrive early for the best ambiance.
meals.lunch: Light refreshments and hot tea at the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (cash only, rustic charm — a true mountain institution since 1927).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Walliser Stube Wine Bar at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — intimate Swiss-inspired fondue and wine bar with an exceptional Alpine cheese fondue, raclette, and curated European wine list. A true mountain luxury experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers trail is 14 km round trip with 365 m elevation gain — wear proper hiking boots and bring trekking poles. The teahouse is cash only and opens mid-June through early October. Afternoon tea at the Chateau Lake Louise should be reserved in advance through the hotel concierge. Canoe rentals at the Fairmont boathouse are first-come, first-served — aim to arrive by 13:30.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Icewalk — Depart by 08:30 for Johnston Canyon, located 26 km west of Banff along the Bow Valley Parkway (a scenic alternate route to the Trans-Canada). Walk the dramatic canyon trail along suspended catwalks bolted into the limestone cliff faces, passing the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). The canyon walls tower overhead and the roaring waterfalls are spectacular. Continue to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs that bubble up from the ground in vivid blue-green hues — for the full 11 km round-trip experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return drive along the Bow Valley Parkway, stop at Castle Mountain Viewpoint and Vermilion Lakes for wildlife spotting (elk, deer, and beaver are commonly sighted) and photography. Return to Banff for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity campus for a cultural interlude, or indulge in a full spa afternoon at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or stroll to the Tunnel Mountain Summit (2.5 km round trip, easy) for 360-degree panoramic views of the Bow Valley, Mount Rundle, and the town of Banff glowing in the golden hour light.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge — fuel up before the canyon hike.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Johnston Canyon Resort Restaurant or a gourmet packed lunch from the hotel enjoyed at the Ink Pots meadow.
meals.dinner: Dinner at 1888 Chop House at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — Alberta's premier steakhouse featuring AAAA-certified Alberta beef, dry-aged cuts, and an extensive wine cellar in an elegant castle-like setting. One of the finest dining experiences in the Canadian Rockies.

day_by_day.notes: The Bow Valley Parkway is one of Canada's most scenic drives and is closed to vehicles from 08:00–11:00 in certain sections during wildlife protection seasons (check Parks Canada for current restrictions). Bear spray is recommended on the Ink Pots extension. Johnston Canyon can be busy by mid-morning on weekends — an early start is strongly advised. The Tunnel Mountain evening hike requires no special gear and takes approximately 45–60 minutes round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Scenic Drive & Athabasca Glacier Walk — Depart by 07:00 for a full-day private guided drive along the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93), widely considered one of the most spectacular roads in the world. Travel north through Banff and Jasper National Parks, stopping at Bow Lake, Peyto Lake Viewpoint (a stunning wolf-head shaped turquoise lake set among the peaks), Mistaya Canyon, and the Saskatchewan River Crossing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre and board the Ice Explorer — a specially designed all-terrain vehicle — for a guided walk onto the Athabasca Glacier, part of the Columbia Icefield, the largest non-polar icefield in North America. Walk on ancient glacial ice and learn about climate change impacts on this iconic landscape. Optionally, visit the Glacier Skywalk — a glass-floored observation platform cantilevered 280 m above the Sunwapta Valley floor. Begin the scenic return drive south along the Parkway in the golden afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 19:00. Enjoy a celebratory dinner at the hotel's finest on-site restaurant or a top Banff establishment, reflecting on the day's extraordinary landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Early in-room breakfast or a packed gourmet breakfast box from the hotel to enjoy at Bow Lake.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Num-Ti-Jah Lodge at Bow Lake — a historic red-roofed lodge on the shores of Bow Lake with stunning mountain views and hearty Canadian fare. A beloved Parkway institution.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Juniper Bistro at the Juniper Hotel — a hidden gem with sweeping panoramic views of the Bow Valley and Mount Norquay, serving refined contemporary Canadian cuisine with a focus on local and seasonal ingredients. A quieter, more intimate alternative to the larger hotel restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway is 232 km one-way from Banff to Jasper — this itinerary covers the southern portion to the Columbia Icefield and returns the same day (approximately 450 km round trip). A private driver or guided vehicle is highly recommended to maximize sightseeing without driving fatigue. Book the Ice Explorer and Glacier Skywalk in advance through Pursuit (the official operator). Dress in warm layers — the glacier is cold and windy regardless of summer temperatures. Fuel up in Lake Louise as services are extremely limited along the Parkway.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk Hike — Begin the final full morning with a ride on the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain (2,281 m). Enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges from the enclosed eight-person gondola cabins. At the summit, walk the 1 km elevated boardwalk to Sanson's Peak, a National Historic Site and former meteorological station, for the most expansive views of the entire Bow Valley. For the adventurous, hike down the Sulphur Mountain Trail (5.5 km, moderate descent) rather than taking the gondola back down.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a leisurely final afternoon. Visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site — the birthplace of Canada's national parks system — for a fascinating cultural and natural history experience. Enjoy a final stroll along the Bow River and through the charming streets of Banff town. Browse luxury outfitters such as Lululemon, Arc'teryx, and local artisan galleries for meaningful souvenirs. Begin packing and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest table in Banff, savoring the last mountain views before the journey home. Check out logistics and arrange private transfer to Calgary Airport for the following morning if needed.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at Sky Bistro atop Sulphur Mountain — dine with panoramic mountain views before or after the boardwalk walk. One of the most spectacular breakfast settings in Canada.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tooloulou's — a beloved Banff institution with a lively atmosphere, serving elevated Cajun-inspired comfort food and craft cocktails in a relaxed setting. A perfect contrast to the fine dining of the week.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at The Vermillion Room at the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel — the hotel's signature dining room set inside the legendary castle, offering an elegant prix-fixe menu of Canadian cuisine with impeccable service, live piano, and unforgettable castle ambiance. The perfect send-off for a luxury Banff experience.

day_by_day.notes: The Banff Gondola opens at 08:00 in summer — arriving early avoids queues and ensures the clearest morning views before any afternoon clouds build. The gondola summit experience takes approximately 2–3 hours including the boardwalk. Confirm checkout time with Banff Mountain Lodge and arrange luggage storage if the afternoon is needed for final exploration. Calgary Airport is approximately 1.5 hours from Banff — plan transfers accordingly and allow extra time for security during peak summer travel season.
